Summary: Subject Definition & Identity Management
Description: Create and maintain the authoritative reusable subject master: identity, department ownership, credits and contact hours. Satisfies FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, BR-01, BR-05, BR-08.

Summary: Create a new subject
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create a new reusable subject under an authorized institution/department, so that a governed subject master exists that ACD-02, ACD-05, EXM, LMS and ACD-10 can reference consistently.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am an authenticated Academic Admin with SUBJECT_CREATE permission, When I POST /api/v1/academics/subjects with subjectCode, name, departmentId, campusId, subjectType, classification, credits, contactHours, elective and academicYear, Then a new subjects document is persisted with status=ACTIVE (or DRAFT per governance policy) and an initial subject_versions document at version=1, And a SubjectCreated event is written to the outbox, And the response returns subjectId, version and status per the Standard Response envelope (FR-01, UC-01, sample §29.1/29.2).

Summary: Enforce institution-scoped subject-code uniqueness
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to enforce that subjectCode is unique within tenant + institution, so that duplicate subject identities can never exist.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subjectCode already exists within the tenant + institution, When a create or code-change request is submitted with the same code, Then the request is rejected with ACD_SUBJECT_CODE_DUPLICATE (409) and no document is written, And campus-level duplicates are permitted only where explicit institutional policy allows it (BR-01, Error Response §29.3).

Summary: Require a subject to be associated with a department
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to require every subject to be associated with a valid, active department, so that ownership and scope are always governed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a departmentId is supplied on create or update, When the service validates it against Department reference data, Then the request succeeds only if the department exists and is active, otherwise a 422 validation error is returned, consistent with 'Subjects must be associated with a department' (Key Business Rules panel 12, BR-08).

Summary: Update a subject's current master fields
Description: As an Academic Admin or Department Head, I want to update the current master fields of a subject (name, department, campus), so that I can correct or refine details without going through full versioning for non-material changes.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold SUBJECT_EDIT permission scoped to the subject's department, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id} with changed fields, Then the master fields are updated with optimistic concurrency enforced, and a SubjectUpdated event is emitted (UC-04, BR-12).

Summary: View subject detail
Description: As an authorized user (Faculty, Student, Department Head, Management), I want to retrieve the full detail of a specific subject, so that I can review its current authoritative definition.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a valid subjectId and a user with SUBJECT_VIEW permission scoped appropriately, When GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id} is called, Then the current subject document is returned with HTTP 200, scoped per the RBAC matrix (§48, UC-02).

Summary: Prevent hard deletion of a referenced or in-use subject
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to reject hard deletion of a subject that is referenced by curriculum or has active batch usage, so that referential integrity is never broken.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject is referenced in curriculum or has active batch offerings, When a hard-delete request is attempted, Then it is rejected with a 409 Conflict, consistent with 'Cannot delete subject if used in curriculum or active batches' (Key Business Rules panel 12, BR-05, Exceptions §15).

Summary: Subject Classification & Taxonomy
Description: Validate and maintain subject type, classification (Theory/Practical/Tutorial/Project/Elective/Audit) and credit/contact-hour policy against configured taxonomy. Satisfies FR-04, FR-05, BR-02, BR-03, BR-04.

Summary: Validate subject type against configured taxonomy
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to validate subjectType against the institution's configured taxonomy on create and update, so that only recognized categories can ever be assigned.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subjectType is submitted that is not part of the configured taxonomy, When the create/update request is validated, Then it is rejected with a 422 validation error, consistent with 'Invalid subject type' (Exceptions §15, BR-04).

Summary: Classify a subject as Theory, Practical, Tutorial, Project, Elective or Audit
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to classify a subject using the institution's defined category set (Theory, Practical, Tutorial, Project, Elective, Audit), so that downstream modules can apply category-specific rules.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a classification value is submitted, When it matches one of the configured categories (Subject Types & Categories panel 5 of the diagram: TH, PR, TU, PJ, EL, AU), Then the subject is classified accordingly and the value is retained for search/filter (FR-05).

Summary: Validate credits and contact hours against institutional policy
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to validate that credits fall within the configured institutional range and contactHours is non-negative and compliant with subject-type policy, so that no subject can be published with an invalid academic weight.
Acceptance Criteria: Given credits or contactHours violate the configured policy for the subject's type/programme, When a create, update or publish action is attempted, Then it is rejected with a 422 validation error, consistent with 'Credit range and subject type must be valid for program' (Key Business Rules panel 12, BR-02, BR-03).

Summary: Mark a subject as elective
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to flag a subject as elective, so that curriculum and enrollment modules can apply elective-specific eligibility and grouping rules.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the elective flag is submitted on create/update, Then the subject's elective indicator is persisted and returned in subsequent reads (Domain Model panel 6, sample request §29.1).

Summary: Subject Catalog & Search
Description: Provide indexed, filterable, paginated search across subjects, and a published catalog view for downstream/public consumption. Satisfies FR-09.

Summary: Search and filter subjects
Description: As an authorized user, I want to search and filter subjects by code, name, type, department and status with pagination, so that I can quickly find the relevant subject in a large master catalog.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/search with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then results are returned within the P95 <2 sec target using indexed queries, and only fields appropriate to my role/classification are included (FR-09, Monitoring §52).

Summary: Retrieve the published subject catalog
Description: As a Student, Faculty or external portal, I want to retrieve the published subject catalog, so that I only see active, catalog-visible subjects.
Acceptance Criteria: Given one or more subjects are ACTIVE and catalog-visible, When GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/catalog is called, Then only published/active subjects are returned, excluding DRAFT/DEPRECATED/RETIRED subjects (API Design panel 3, RBAC 'View published subjects (read-only)').

Summary: List subjects by category or department
Description: As an authorized user, I want to list subjects filtered by category or department, so that I can browse the subject catalog in a structured way.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/subjects/category/{category} or /api/v1/subjects/department/{deptId}, When the request is processed, Then all matching active subjects are returned via an indexed lookup (API Design panel 3 of the diagram).

Summary: Subject Version Management
Description: Create, publish and reconstruct immutable, monotonically-numbered subject versions so historical academic definitions are always reconstructable. Satisfies FR-06, FR-07, BR-06, BR-07, BR-10.

Summary: Create a new subject version
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create a new draft version of a subject, so that academic changes can be prepared and reviewed before publication without disturbing the currently effective definition.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject exists, When I POST /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions, Then a new subject_versions document is created in DRAFT status with the next monotonic version number, and a SubjectVersionCreated event is emitted (FR-06, UC-05, BR-10).

Summary: Update a draft subject version
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to update the fields of a subject version while it is still DRAFT, so that I can refine it before publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject_versions document is in status=DRAFT, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions/{v} with changed fields, Then the draft is updated in place, and attempting the same update once the version is PUBLISHED is rejected with a 409 immutable-resource error (FR-07, BR-06, Exceptions §15).

Summary: Publish a subject version
Description: As an Authorized Approver, I want to publish a prepared subject version, so that it becomes the effective, catalog-visible definition for that subject.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a version has passed validation, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions/{v}/publish, Then the version's status becomes PUBLISHED, the prior published version is marked SUPERSEDED, and SubjectVersionPublished + SubjectVersionSuperseded events are emitted (UC-06, Event Contracts §31).

Summary: Prevent mutation of published versions
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to reject any attempt to modify a published subject_versions document, so that historical reconstruction always remains trustworthy.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject_versions document has status=PUBLISHED, When any update operation targets that document directly, Then the operation is rejected at the application and repository layer (BR-06, 'Published subjects are immutable (use versioning)' — Key Business Rules panel 12).

Summary: Enforce monotonic, never-reused version numbers
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want version numbers to increase monotonically and never be reused for a given subject, so that version history is always unambiguous.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject already has one or more versions, When a new version is created, Then it is assigned the next sequential number, and no prior version number can ever be reassigned (BR-10).

Summary: Retrieve version history for a subject
Description: As an authorized user, I want to list all versions of a subject, so that I can review how it has evolved over time.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subjectId with one or more versions, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions, Then all versions are returned ordered by version number with status and effective dates.

Summary: Retrieve a specific historical subject version
Description: As an authorized user, I want to fetch a specific past version of a subject, so that I can reconstruct exactly what was in effect at a prior point in time.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subjectId and a version number that exists, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/versions/{v}, Then the immutable snapshot for that version is returned unchanged from when it was published (BR-06).

Summary: Reject stale writes with optimistic version locking
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to detect when a client submits an update based on a stale version, so that two concurrent edits can never silently overwrite each other.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a client submits an update based on a stale version reference, When the write is attempted, Then it is rejected with a 409 optimistic-concurrency error instructing the client to reload the latest version (BR-12, Exceptions §15 'Stale version').

Summary: Subject Metadata Management
Description: Maintain optional extended academic metadata (tags, delivery mode, assessment mode, regulatory codes, industry relevance, language) separately from the core subject aggregate. Satisfies §39 subject_metadata.

Summary: Add or update extended metadata for a subject
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to attach extended academic metadata (tags, delivery mode, assessment mode, regulatory code, industry relevance, language of instruction) to a subject, so that richer academic context is available without destabilizing the core subject record.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject exists, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/metadata with the metadata fields, Then a subject_metadata document is created/updated (one per subject, enforced by a unique tenantId+subjectId index), and regulatory fields require elevated permission to set (Field-Level Data Dictionary §39, Validation Rules).

Summary: Retrieve extended metadata for a subject
Description: As Faculty or an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve the extended metadata for a subject, so that I can see its tags, delivery mode, assessment mode and other academic context alongside the core definition.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject has metadata recorded, When GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/metadata is called, Then the metadata document is returned, with L3 fields (regulatoryCode, prerequisiteNotes) filtered per the requester's classification clearance.

Summary: Search subjects by metadata tag
Description: As an authorized user, I want to search subjects by academic tag, so that I can discover subjects within a thematic grouping beyond exact code/name matching.
Acceptance Criteria: Given subjects have been tagged via subject_metadata, When I search using a tag filter, Then matching subjects are returned via the multikey tenantId+tags index (Indexes §39).

Summary: Subject Prerequisite & Co-requisite Management
Description: Maintain the authoritative subject-to-subject prerequisite/co-requisite graph with cycle detection, minimum-grade rules and impact analysis. Satisfies §39 subject_prerequisites.

Summary: Add a subject prerequisite or co-requisite
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to add a prerequisite or co-requisite relationship between two subjects (with mandatory flag and minimum grade), so that eligibility rules can be enforced consistently by curriculum and enrollment modules.
Acceptance Criteria: Given both subjects exist, belong to the same permitted scope, and subjectId does not equal prerequisiteSubjectId, When I POST /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/prerequisites with prerequisiteSubjectId, relationshipType, mandatory and minimumGrade, Then the relationship is validated for cycles and persisted, and a SubjectPrerequisiteAdded event is emitted (subject_prerequisites §39, Event Contracts §31).

Summary: Reject prerequisite cycles
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to detect and reject any prerequisite relationship that would create a cycle in the prerequisite graph, so that eligibility logic downstream never enters an unresolvable loop.
Acceptance Criteria: Given adding a proposed prerequisite edge would create a cycle in the directed prerequisite graph, When the add-prerequisite request is validated, Then it is rejected with a 409 error, consistent with 'No circular prerequisite dependencies' (Key Business Rules panel 12, Failure Handling panel 13).

Summary: Prevent duplicate active prerequisite relationships
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to reject a duplicate active prerequisite relationship between the same subject pair, so that the dependency graph stays unambiguous.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an active prerequisite relationship already exists between subjectId and prerequisiteSubjectId, When the same relationship is submitted again, Then it is rejected, consistent with 'Duplicate active relationships are prohibited' (Integrity/Consistency Rules §39).

Summary: Block deactivated subjects from being newly introduced as prerequisites
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to reject adding a deactivated subject as a new prerequisite unless policy explicitly permits it, so that active subjects never depend on an unavailable subject.
Acceptance Criteria: Given prerequisiteSubjectId refers to a deactivated subject, When an add-prerequisite request is submitted without an explicit policy exception, Then it is rejected, consistent with 'deactivated subjects cannot be introduced as new prerequisites unless policy explicitly permits it' (Integrity/Consistency Rules §39).

Summary: Remove a subject prerequisite
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to remove an existing prerequisite relationship, so that I can correct or retire an obsolete eligibility rule.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an active prerequisite relationship exists, When I call DELETE on the prerequisite resource, Then the relationship is deactivated/retired (not hard-deleted) and a SubjectPrerequisiteRemoved event is emitted, and historical relationships are retained for reconstruction (Retention/Lifecycle §39).

Summary: List forward and reverse prerequisite dependencies for a subject
Description: As an authorized user, I want to view both the prerequisites a subject depends on and the subjects that depend on it, so that I can perform impact analysis before changing or deactivating a subject.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subjectId, When I query its prerequisite graph, Then forward lookups (by subjectId) and reverse dependency lookups (by prerequisiteSubjectId) are both supported via indexed graph traversal, bounded by policy (Query/Aggregation Considerations §39).

Summary: Subject Lifecycle Governance
Description: Govern the full subject lifecycle state machine — active, deprecated, deactivated, reactivated, retired — without ever deleting historical evidence. Satisfies FR-08, BR-09, BR-11, BR-13, UC-07/08.

Summary: Deactivate a subject
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to deactivate a subject, so that new usage is blocked while its full history is retained.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject is in an eligible lifecycle state, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/deactivate, Then the status transitions to DEACTIVATED, a SubjectDeactivated event is emitted, new usage (curriculum mapping, batch allocation) is blocked, and no historical data is deleted (FR-08, UC-07, BR-09).

Summary: Reactivate a subject
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to reactivate a deactivated subject where policy permits, so that it can resume normal availability for curriculum and timetable use.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject is in status=DEACTIVATED and reactivation is permitted by policy, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/reactivate, Then the status transitions back to ACTIVE and a SubjectReactivated event is emitted (UC-08, Subject Lifecycle §13).

Summary: Mark a subject as deprecated
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to mark a subject as deprecated, so that it is signaled for phase-out while still permitted for existing academic references.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject is ACTIVE, When a deprecate transition is invoked, Then the status transitions to DEPRECATED and a SubjectDeprecated event is emitted (Subject Lifecycle §13, Event Contracts §31).

Summary: Retire a subject permanently
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to retire a subject from new usage, so that it is permanently closed to new academic assignment while remaining queryable for audit and historical reconstruction.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject is DEPRECATED or DEACTIVATED, When a retire transition is invoked, Then the status transitions to RETIRED and a SubjectRetired event is emitted, consistent with the version-lifecycle terminal state (Subject Lifecycle §13).

Summary: Block new curriculum mapping of a deprecated/deactivated subject
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to reject new curriculum mappings for a deprecated or deactivated subject unless policy explicitly permits it, so that new academic structures are never built on a subject being phased out.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject is DEPRECATED or DEACTIVATED, When ACD-02 attempts to map it as a new curriculum subject without an explicit policy exception, Then the reference validation call returns rejection, consistent with BR-11.

Summary: Update controlled lifecycle status via a single governed endpoint
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to transition a subject's lifecycle status through a single governed endpoint, so that every lifecycle change is validated and audited consistently regardless of which specific transition is requested.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a requested status transition, When I call PUT /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/status, Then the transition is validated against the allowed lifecycle state machine, the status is updated, and the change is recorded in history (API Design §28, Activity — Subject Lifecycle §26).

Summary: Retrieve change history for a subject
Description: As an authorized user or Auditor, I want to retrieve the full change history for a subject, so that I can review every lifecycle transition, update and who performed it.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject has one or more history entries, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/subjects/{id}/history, Then all history entries are returned in chronological order with actor and timestamp (UC-09, API Design §28).

Summary: Bulk Import & Export
Description: Support bulk import and export of the subject catalog with per-row validation and duplicate handling. Satisfies the diagram's bulk import/export endpoints and UC-10.

Summary: Bulk import subjects
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to bulk import subjects from a file, so that I can migrate or synchronize a large subject catalog efficiently during onboarding or data correction.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a properly formatted bulk import file, When it is submitted via POST /api/v1/subjects/import, Then each row is validated against the same business rules as a single create (code uniqueness, department, credits, taxonomy), row-level errors are reported without aborting the whole batch, and duplicates are detected and handled per policy, consistent with 'Bulk import must validate data and handle duplicates' (Key Business Rules panel 12).

Summary: Export the subject catalog
Description: As an authorized user, I want to export the subject catalog, so that I can share or archive it outside the platform.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold SUBJECT_EXPORT permission, When I call GET /api/v1/subjects/export, Then a CSV/Excel export of the current catalog is produced consistent with my role's field visibility, matching UC-10 (Export Catalog) and the diagram's /export endpoint.

Summary: Event-Driven Integration
Description: Reliably publish the full subject domain event catalog via a transactional outbox and consume upstream Department/Course events, so ACD-02, ACD-05, EXM, LMS and ACD-10 stay eventually consistent. Satisfies FR-10, FR-11.

Summary: Publish domain events via transactional outbox
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want every state-changing operation to write its domain event (SubjectCreated, SubjectUpdated, SubjectVersionCreated, SubjectVersionPublished, SubjectVersionSuperseded, SubjectDeactivated, SubjectReactivated, SubjectDeprecated, SubjectRetired, SubjectPrerequisiteAdded, SubjectPrerequisiteRemoved, SubjectCatalogPublished) to a transactional outbox in the same transaction as the business write, so events are never lost even if the broker is temporarily unavailable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject create/version/lifecycle/prerequisite operation commits successfully, When the transaction completes, Then the corresponding event from the Event Contracts catalog (§31) is durably recorded in outbox_events within the same transaction and relayed to Kafka/RabbitMQ with retry until acknowledged (Event Architecture §30, FR-14).

Summary: Consume DepartmentUpdated and DepartmentDeactivated events
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to consume DepartmentUpdated and DepartmentDeactivated events, so that subject department-reference context stays current and affected subjects are flagged when their department is deactivated.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a DepartmentUpdated or DepartmentDeactivated event is received for a departmentId referenced by one or more subjects, When the event is processed, Then reference context is refreshed or affected subjects are flagged/restricted respectively, without overwriting the authoritative department master (Event Consumption §33, FR-11).

Summary: Consume CourseUpdated and CourseDeactivated events
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to consume CourseUpdated and CourseDeactivated events from ACD-01, so that any optional course-reference context on a subject stays current and affected subjects are flagged if policy links them to a deactivated course.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a CourseUpdated or CourseDeactivated event is received, When the event is processed, Then the optional course-reference context is refreshed, or affected subjects are flagged where policy links them to that course (Event Consumption §33).

Summary: Deduplicate inbound events using eventId
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want to deduplicate inbound events by eventId, so that redelivered or replayed events never cause duplicate side effects.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound event with an eventId already processed successfully, When it is redelivered, Then the service recognizes the duplicate and skips reprocessing without error (Event Consumption §33).

Summary: Route unprocessable events to a dead-letter queue
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want events that repeatedly fail processing to be routed to a dead-letter queue after retries are exhausted, so that they can be investigated and replayed without blocking the main stream.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound or outbound event fails processing after the maximum configured retry attempts, When retries are exhausted, Then the event is persisted to dead_letter_events with failure context and an alert is raised (Retry Strategy §54, Monitoring §52).

Summary: Idempotency, Concurrency & Transaction Integrity
Description: Guarantee safe client retries on create/publish/deactivate/reactivate commands and correct concurrent-edit handling across subject, version and history writes. Satisfies FR-14, §54, §55, §56.

Summary: Support idempotent create, publish, deactivate and reactivate requests
Description: As an API client, I want to supply an idempotency key on create/publish/deactivate/reactivate commands, so that a retried request never creates a duplicate subject or duplicate side effect.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a request is retried with the same idempotency key and identical payload, When it is reprocessed, Then the original result is returned without re-executing the write, And the same key with a different payload returns a conflict error (Idempotency §55, FR-14).

Summary: Use MongoDB transactions for coupled subject writes
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want subject, version, history and outbox writes that must succeed or fail together to be wrapped in a MongoDB transaction, so that partial writes never leave the system in an inconsistent state.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject create or publish operation touches subjects, subject_versions, history and outbox_events, When the operation executes, Then all writes commit atomically or none do (Transaction Strategy §56, Event Architecture §30 'Subject State + Version + History + Outbox').

Summary: Security, RBAC & Audit Governance
Description: Enforce the full role-based access matrix (including the diagram's Parent and Auditor roles), classify data sensitivity, and maintain an immutable audit trail. Satisfies FR-12, FR-13, §47-50.

Summary: Enforce the full RBAC permission matrix
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want every endpoint to check the caller's role against the RBAC matrix (Super Admin: all permissions; Academic Admin: create/edit/submit/publish-where-authorized/deactivate; Department Head: create/edit/review within department; Registrar: approve/publish/retire; Faculty: view + edit/submit where assigned; Student: view published/catalog data; Management: view/export where authorized; Service Accounts: scoped reference-read), so that only authorized actors can perform each action.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a user attempts an action without the corresponding permission for their role, When the request reaches the service, Then it is rejected with 401/403 per the Error Handling table (§53) before any business logic executes, and the full matrix in §48 (plus its ABAC examples: tenant/institution/department scope match) is enforced consistently across every endpoint.

Summary: Grant Parent read-only access to their child's subject catalog
Description: As a Parent, I want read-only access to the published subject catalog through the Parent Portal, so that I can view my child's subject information without any ability to modify academic data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as a Parent, When I access subject data via the Parent Portal, Then I receive only published/catalog-visible subject information, strictly read-only, consistent with 'View subject catalog (read-only)' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Grant Auditor read-only access to subject history and audit logs
Description: As an Auditor, I want read-only access to subject history and audit logs across all subjects, so that I can perform compliance reviews without any ability to modify data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold the Auditor role, When I access any subject history/audit endpoint, Then I receive read-only results and any write attempt is rejected, matching 'View subject history and audit logs' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Grant External API consumers scoped read-only access
Description: As an External API consumer, I want read-only access limited to the scope defined for my API key, so that I can consume published subject data without any write capability or over-broad visibility.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call any ACD-03 endpoint, Then I receive only the data within my granted scope and read-only access, matching 'Read-only access (as per scope)' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Record an immutable, append-only history entry for every material change
Description: As a Compliance Officer, I want every lifecycle transition, version publication and correction to be recorded as an append-only history entry, so that a complete, tamper-evident audit trail always exists.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any material mutation occurs (create, update, version, publish, deactivate, reactivate, deprecate, retire, prerequisite change), When the mutation commits, Then a corresponding history record is written capturing action, actorId and timestamp, and history records can never be updated or deleted, consistent with 'All changes must be audited' (Key Business Rules panel 12, Audit Model §46).

Summary: Classify and protect subject data by sensitivity level
Description: As a Security Architect, I want subject data classified into L1 Public, L2 Internal, L3 Confidential and L4 Highly Restricted tiers, so that access controls and exposure match each field's sensitivity.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a field is classified L3 (approval/actor/regulatory/audit details) or L4 (operational/idempotency/DLQ data), When a user without sufficient clearance queries subject data, Then those fields are excluded from the response while L1 catalog fields remain visible per role (Data Classification §49).

Summary: Encrypt subject data at rest and in transit
Description: As a Security Architect, I want all ACD-03 service communication encrypted in transit (TLS) and MongoDB data encrypted at rest, so that subject data is protected against interception and storage compromise.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-03 is deployed to any environment, When traffic flows between clients, the API gateway and MongoDB, Then TLS is enforced end-to-end, encryption at rest is enabled, backups are encrypted, and sensitive fields are masked in operational logs (Encryption and Secrets §50).

Summary: Observability, Reliability & Performance
Description: Provide structured logging, metrics, tracing, alerting and defined SLOs so operations can detect, diagnose and recover from failures quickly. Satisfies §51-54, §57-59.

Summary: Emit structured logs with correlation context
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want every ACD-03 request to emit a structured log with timestamp, service, tenantId, requestId, correlationId, actorId, operation and outcome, so that I can trace any request end-to-end across services.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any API call to ACD-03, When the request completes (success or failure), Then a structured log entry containing all required fields is emitted with no secrets/bearer tokens present, and correlationId propagates through event headers (Logging and Observability §51).

Summary: Expose operational metrics and distributed tracing
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want request rate, latency, error rate, DB latency, cache hit rate and event backlog exposed as metrics, plus end-to-end tracing from Gateway through ACD-03 to MongoDB/outbox/broker/consumers, so that I can monitor service health and diagnose latency issues.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-03 is running in production, When metrics are scraped and traces are sampled, Then all listed metrics are available on the monitoring dashboard and a trace can be followed across the full request path (§51).

Summary: Alert on SLO-breaching and reliability signals
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want alerts configured for API P95 >300ms, search P95 >2s, elevated 5xx rate, MongoDB latency, outbox backlog growth, DLQ open count, cache-hit-ratio degradation and event lag, so that incidents are caught before they impact users.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any monitored signal crosses its defined threshold, When the breach is sustained beyond the alerting window, Then an alert fires to the on-call channel with enough context to begin triage (Monitoring and Alerting §52).

Summary: Apply bounded retry with exponential backoff for transient failures
Description: As the Subject Management Service, I want transient failures (broker unavailable, MongoDB timeout, dependency latency) to be retried with exponential backoff and jitter up to a bounded limit, so that temporary issues self-heal without manual intervention or infinite retry storms.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a transient failure occurs on a retryable operation, When the retry policy executes, Then attempts back off exponentially with jitter up to a maximum bound, and deterministic validation failures are never retried (Retry Strategy §54).

Summary: Meet indexed read/write performance targets
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want subject detail reads, catalog search, create/update writes and version/prerequisite lookups to meet their defined latency targets via proper indexing, so the service remains responsive at institutional scale.
Acceptance Criteria: Given production-representative load, When each workload type is exercised, Then API P95 stays within the documented threshold and search P95 stays under 2s, verified in performance testing (NFR §16, Performance §59, MongoDB Index Strategy §43).

Summary: Validate disaster recovery via regular restore tests
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want automated MongoDB backups with tested restore procedures, so that ACD-03 can meet its defined RPO/RTO in a disaster scenario.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the configured backup schedule, When a scheduled restore test is executed against a non-production environment, Then the restored dataset is verified complete and consistent (Disaster Recovery and Backup §57).

Summary: API Standards, Error Handling & Contracts
Description: Deliver a consistent, versioned REST contract with standardized request/response envelopes and the full documented error taxonomy across all ACD-03 endpoints. Cross-cutting.

Summary: Publish and version the ACD-03 API contract
Description: As an API Consumer, I want a versioned specification covering every /api/v1/academics/subjects endpoint (create, list/search, detail, update, catalog, versions, version detail/update, publish, deactivate, reactivate, status, history), so that I can integrate against a stable, documented contract.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-03 service, When the API contract is published, Then it documents every endpoint in the REST API Specification (§28) with request/response schemas, and breaking changes require a new API version.

Summary: Return standardized success and error envelopes
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every response to follow the standard {success, data, meta} / {success:false, error, meta} envelope with requestId and correlationId, so that clients can handle responses uniformly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any ACD-03 API call, When the response is returned, Then it conforms to the Standard Response / Error Response shapes in §29.2/29.3.

Summary: Map every documented failure family to its specified HTTP status
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every failure family (malformed request, authentication, authorization, not found, conflict, business validation, rate limit, internal error, dependency unavailable) mapped to its documented HTTP status, so that I can build reliable client-side error handling.
Acceptance Criteria: Given each documented failure condition occurs, When the API responds, Then it returns exactly the status defined in the Error Handling table (§53): 400 malformed/business-validation-adjacent, 401 authentication, 403 authorization, 404 not found, 409 conflict (duplicate/stale/immutable), 422 business validation, 429 rate limit, 500 internal, 503 dependency unavailable.

Summary: End-to-End Scenarios & Cross-Module Integration
Description: Validate complete cross-cutting flows spanning creation, metadata, prerequisites, approval, publication and every listed downstream module integration (ACD-01, ACD-02, ACD-04, ACD-05, EXM, STM, HRM, COM, ACD-10). Satisfies Testing Strategy §67 and Cross-Module Integration panel 11.

Summary: E2E: Create → Add Metadata → Define Prerequisites → Review → Approve → Activate/Publish
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test that follows the full sample workflow (Create Subject Draft, Add Metadata, Define Prerequisites, Department Review, Academic Admin Approval, Activate/Publish), so that the complete authoritative-subject lifecycle is proven to work together exactly as designed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a fresh subject is created via UC-01, When it proceeds through metadata addition, prerequisite definition, department review and approval, and is then published/activated, Then the resulting SubjectCreated/SubjectVersionPublished/SubjectCatalogPublished events are observed, verified end-to-end (Sample Workflow panel 14 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: E2E: subject used in curriculum and timetable after activation
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test proving a newly activated subject becomes usable in ACD-02 (Curriculum) and ACD-05 (Timetable), so that the downstream 'Use in Curriculum' / 'Use in Timetable' steps of the sample workflow are continuously verified.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject has been activated/published, When ACD-02 maps it into a curriculum and ACD-05 schedules it into a timetable, Then both operations succeed and reflect the subject's current published definition (Sample Workflow panel 14, Cross-Module Integration panel 11).

Summary: E2E: deactivation blocked while subject is in active curriculum/batch use
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test proving a subject cannot be hard-deleted while referenced in curriculum or active batches, and that deactivation instead blocks new usage while preserving history, so that the cross-collection business rule is continuously verified.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject is referenced by an active curriculum mapping, When a hard-delete is attempted (rejected with 409) and a deactivate is then performed instead, Then deactivation succeeds, new curriculum/batch usage is blocked, and existing references remain intact (Key Business Rules panel 12, Failure Handling panel 13).

Summary: Validate integrations with ACD-01, ACD-02, ACD-04, ACD-05, EXM, STM, HRM, COM and ACD-10 before production sign-off
Description: As a Release Manager, I want end-to-end integration tests against every module listed in the Cross-Module Integration table executed as part of the Production Definition of Done, so that ACD-03 is not released until its downstream contracts are proven.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-03 release candidate, When the full integration suite runs against ACD-01 (map subjects to courses), ACD-02 (use subjects in curriculum), ACD-04 (subject allocation to batch), ACD-05 (subject availability & scheduling), EXM (subject scheme & assessment), STM (subject enrollment & records), HRM (faculty subject assignment), COM (notify subject updates) and ACD-10 (subject analytics & insights), Then all contract, event-schema and E2E scenarios pass, and this gate is required before the service is marked production-ready (Production Definition of Done §68, Cross-Module Integration panel 11).
